payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-13
payload.summary:
**Anthropic** spent the day explaining itself: Claude Code regressions came from product-layer changes, not the API; Managed Agents kept expanding with cleaner abstractions, self-hosted sandboxes, and private **MCP** access; **builder mood turned jumpy** as posts about **Fable**, ID checks, and model controls dragged regulation and geopolitics straight into the dev timeline; shipping did not slow down, though, with **HarnessAgent**, Codex UX tweaks, benchmark talk, and founders describing agents that now run for days instead of demos for minutes.

**Anthropic** 这波先灭火再推新品：Claude Code 变差不是模型突然塌了，而是产品层几处改动叠出来的；Managed Agents 也没停，接口拆得更干净，还把自托管沙箱和私有 **MCP** 通道放了出来；X 上的气氛就没这么平，**Fable**、身份验证、模型管制混在一起，开发者时间线一股火药味；另一边大家照样猛干，**HarnessAgent**、Codex 小改动、基准测试、还有那种一跑就是几天的 agent 工作流，已经不是演示味了。

sections.headline: Coding agents stretch out; open weights wobble; API economics get questioned / 编码 agent 越跑越长；开放权重开始发虚；API 生意也被拿出来重问
sections.body:
Jacob Efron, Ari from **Datalogy**, and Rob from **Radical** frame this episode as an AI "vibe check" and land on a few hard themes: coding agents are finally useful over longer time horizons, engineers are starting to manage agents instead of only writing code themselves, and that shift is driving both higher output and more review debt. They also argue that open-weight frontier models may be retreating for economic and geopolitical reasons, while enterprise buyers are getting much more cost-sensitive as long-running models burn through tokens.

Most of the energy comes from the friction, not the hype. Ari says stronger coding agents make it easier to flood a codebase with work you do not fully understand; Rob questions whether frontier open models stay viable at all; and the group floats a sharper claim that some labs may eventually de-emphasize APIs if compute remains tight. The throughline is simple: capability is still rising, but cost, harness design, and product form factors are now steering the conversation almost as much as raw model quality.

Jacob Efron、**Datalogy** 的 Ari 和 **Radical** 的 Rob 把这期节目做成了一次 AI "vibe check"，几刀都砍在要害上：编码 agent 终于能在更长任务上派上用场，工程师开始更像是在带 agent 干活，而不只是自己敲代码；随之而来的不是纯增益，还多了审查压力和理解断层。他们还聊到开放权重前沿模型可能因为商业账和地缘因素往回收，而企业客户对成本突然变得很敏感，长时推理一跑，token 账单就炸出来了。

这期最好听的地方恰恰是那点不舒服。Ari 直说，agent 变强以后，往代码库里灌一大坨你自己都没吃透的东西，实在太容易了；Rob 则怀疑前沿开放模型这条路还能不能撑下去；几个人甚至把话挑明，说如果算力一直紧，实验室迟早会重新想 API 这门生意。意思很清楚：能力还在涨，但现在真正卡脖子的，越来越是成本、harness 设计和产品形态，不只是模型分数。

sections.headline: **Anthropic** traces Claude Code quality complaints to three product-layer changes / **Anthropic** 把 Claude Code 口碑下滑追到了三处产品层改动
sections.body:
**Anthropic** says recent Claude Code degradation reports did not come from the API or inference layer. The post identifies three separate causes: lowering default reasoning effort from high to medium on March 4, a March 26 caching bug that repeatedly cleared prior reasoning after idle sessions, and an April 16 prompt change meant to reduce verbosity that hurt coding quality. All three issues were rolled back or fixed by April 20, with the major cache bug fixed in v2.1.101 and the broader set resolved in v2.1.116.

The interesting part is what failed around the failures. Internal evals did not catch the issues cleanly, the broken behavior was hard to reproduce, and different slices of traffic saw different regressions at different times, which made the overall pattern look noisy. **Anthropic** says it is resetting subscriber usage limits and changing its review process, including expanding code review context after **Opus 4.7** could find the offending bug while **Opus 4.6** could not.

**Anthropic** 这篇基本是在做技术复盘：最近大家觉得 Claude Code 变笨，不是 API 层或者推理层出了问题，而是三处产品层改动叠在了一起。第一处是 3 月 4 日把默认 reasoning effort 从 high 调成 medium；第二处是 3 月 26 日上的缓存优化出了 bug，闲置会话恢复后会反复清掉旧推理；第三处是 4 月 16 日为了让回复别那么啰嗦，加了一条系统提示，结果把写代码质量也带坏了。到 4 月 20 日，这几处都已经回滚或修好，核心缓存 bug 在 v2.1.101 修复，整组问题在 v2.1.116 收尾。

更值得看的是它怎么漏过去的。内部评测一开始没复现干净，问题又卡在比较偏的交叉场景里，不同流量切片还在不同时间中招，所以外面看起来像一团随机波动。**Anthropic** 现在给订阅用户重置额度，也准备改代码审查流程，尤其是补更多仓库上下文进去，因为他们回测时发现，**Opus 4.7** 能抓到那次出事的 bug，**Opus 4.6** 抓不到。

sections.headline: Managed Agents splits the brain, the hands, and the session log / Managed Agents 把大脑、手和会话日志彻底拆开
sections.body:
**Anthropic** describes Managed Agents as a hosted system for long-running agents built around three durable interfaces: the session, the harness, and the sandbox. The post argues that earlier all-in-one container designs created "pets" that were fragile to debug, hard to recover, and awkward to connect to customer infrastructure. By moving the harness outside the execution container and treating tools and sandboxes as replaceable components, the system can restart pieces independently and recover from failures by replaying the session log.

Security and context management are the deeper themes. The company says generated code should never sit next to reusable credentials, so Git auth and MCP access are pushed behind safer boundaries. It also treats the session log as durable memory outside the model context window, letting agents reread or slice prior events instead of making one-way truncation decisions too early. The post reads less like a launch note and more like a statement about what agent infrastructure has to look like once tasks stop being toy-sized.

**Anthropic** 这篇不是在讲花活，讲的是架构基本功。Managed Agents 被拆成三个稳定接口：session、harness、sandbox。文章的意思很直接，过去把这些东西全塞进一个容器里，短期省事，长期全是坑，出了问题像在养宠物机，既难查也难救，还不方便接进客户自己的基础设施。现在 harness 被挪出执行容器，工具和沙箱都按可替换部件来对待，哪一段挂了就重启哪一段，再靠 session log 把现场接回来。

真正的重点有两个。第一是安全，模型生成的代码不该和可复用凭证待在一个地方，所以 Git 授权、MCP 调用都被压到更安全的边界后面。第二是上下文，session log 被当成模型上下文窗口之外的持久记忆，agent 需要时可以回读、切片、重看，不用太早做那种一刀切掉就回不来的裁剪。整篇读下来不像产品宣传，更像是在说：任务一旦不再是玩具级，agent 基础设施就得长成这个样子。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents** adds self-hosted sandboxes and private **MCP** tunnels / **Claude Managed Agents** 上线自托管沙箱和私有 **MCP** 通道
sections.body:
**Anthropic** says Managed Agents can now execute tools inside sandboxes customers control and reach private **MCP** servers without exposing them to the public internet. The orchestration loop stays on **Anthropic's** side, but execution moves into infrastructure owned by the customer or a supported provider such as **Cloudflare**, **Daytona**, **Modal**, or **Vercel**. Self-hosted sandboxes are in public beta, while MCP tunnels are in research preview.

The update is mainly about enterprise boundaries. Customers keep files, packages, services, network policy, and audit controls inside their own perimeter, while still using the hosted agent loop. The post also uses partner examples like **Amplitude**, **Clay**, and **Rogo** to show where the feature fits: long builds, design generation, GTM workflows, and finance analysis that need tighter control over data and runtime.

**Anthropic** 这次给 Managed Agents 补上的，是企业最在意的那一块：工具执行现在可以放进客户自己控制的沙箱里，私有 **MCP** 服务也能接进来，而且不用把内网服务直接暴露到公网。编排循环还在 **Anthropic** 那边跑，但真正执行工具的环境可以放在客户自有基础设施里，或者放在 **Cloudflare**、**Daytona**、**Modal**、**Vercel** 这些托管提供商上。自托管沙箱是公测，MCP tunnels 还在 research preview。

说白了，这就是把 agent 往企业边界里面推。文件、依赖、服务、网络策略、审计链路都留在自己地盘里，外面只借用托管的 agent loop。文章里拿 **Amplitude**、**Clay**、**Rogo** 举例，也挺说明问题：长时间构建、设计生成、GTM 工作流、金融分析，这些活不是不能跑 agent，而是你先得把数据和运行时控制住。

sections.headline: Maybe Git is the next legacy bottleneck / 也许下一个该被怀疑的老瓶颈就是 Git
sections.body:
## The Future Codebase

After the PR dies, after the Code Review dies,
i am seriously wondering if Git needs to die next.

roughly 20-40% of code spend is just managing and updating merge conflicts. necessary evil? or legacy "horseless carriage"? cargo culting the past?

we don't do line by line merge conflicts when we collaborate with human colleagues - instead we chat, suggest edits, do side comments, and an owner ships it. 

btw we also don't do CI/CD even collaborating on documents with serious legal/financial implications.

maybe the future codebase looks more like a Notion or Linear database than .git objects. It will be less efficient, but more scalable. exactly the Salty Lesson.

## 未来的代码库

等 PR 死掉之后，等 Code Review 死掉之后，
我是真的开始怀疑，下一个该死的是不是 Git。

大概 20-40% 的代码成本，都花在处理和更新 merge conflict 上。它是必要之恶？还是一种老式的“无马马车”？是在对过去搞形式主义崇拜吗？

我们和人类同事协作时，并不是一行一行地处理 merge conflict，而是聊天、提修改建议、写边注，然后由负责人发出去。

顺便说一句，就算是在协作那些有严肃法律/财务影响的文档时，我们也不会搞 CI/CD。

也许未来的代码库看起来会更像 **Notion** 或 **Linear** 数据库，而不是 `.git` objects。它效率会低一点，但可扩展性更强。完全就是那个 **Salty Lesson**。

sections.headline: Levie calls model controls a regulatory turning point / Levie 认为对模型本身下手，是监管拐点
sections.body:
This is a big turning point for AI regulation.

The government is starting to deem some models too powerful for certain uses, which creates a precedent for a range of possible controls in the future.

I’m in the camp that this is unnecessary and we should be primarily regulating the use of AI, as opposed to the underlying models. But, equally, there are plenty of people that actually prefer this outcome.

Either way, it’s unlikely that we’re going back to a world where the government doesn’t have far more meaningful involvement in the rate of AI progress.

这对 AI 监管来说是个很大的转折点。

政府开始认定某些模型对某些用途来说太强了，这为未来一整套可能的管制方式开了先例。

我属于那一派，觉得这没必要，我们更该监管的是 AI 的使用方式，而不是底层模型本身。但同样也有很多人其实更喜欢这个结果。

不管怎样，我们大概率回不去那个政府不会更深度介入 AI 进展速度的世界了。

sections.headline: AI coding tools can speed up bureaucracy too / AI 编码工具不只加速创造，也会加速官僚化
sections.body:
Everyone thinks AI coding tools set founders free.

Watch what people actually build with them: rules, approvals, process, layers. The same cage, assembled faster.

The tool that can scaffold anything in an afternoon will scaffold your bureaucracy in an afternoon too.

Speed of construction is speed of calcification. Build the thing that lets you create new things: experiences that didn’t happen before.

大家都觉得 AI 编码工具会把创始人解放出来。

但你去看看大家实际上拿它们造了什么：规则、审批、流程、层层结构。还是那个笼子，只是组得更快了。

一个能在一下午里 scaffold 出任何东西的工具，也能在一下午里把你的官僚体系 scaffold 出来。

建造速度，就是钙化速度。去做那种能让你创造新东西的东西：那些以前根本不会发生的体验。

sections.headline: Two voices, one founder brain / 一个人脑子里，常常真有两种声音
sections.body:
Anyone else have two voices?

I often have two voices that come out both in my writing and how I speak. 

One is the frenetic, time is the enemy, direct, punchy gets to the point quickly and then the second is more calm, measured, structured inquisitive, trying to peel the layers. 

They are distinctive enough that people think it’s two different people (especially in writing). 

They are usually separate but I feel I often oscillate between the two in the same conversation.

还有别人也会有两种声音吗？

我经常有两种声音，不管在写东西还是说话时都会冒出来。

一种很躁，觉得时间是敌人，直接、短促、很快切到重点；另一种更平静、更克制、更有结构，也更爱追问，想把层层东西剥开。

它们明显到别人会以为这是两个人，尤其是在文字里。

平时这两种声音大多分开，但我感觉自己经常会在同一场对话里来回切换。

sections.headline: Codex inside crabbox turns into nonstop self-building infra / Codex 在 crabbox 里一边构建一边干活，已经像自我生长的基础设施
sections.body:
I can barely keep up with implementing/testing/landing all the Issues/PRs folks submit to https://t.co/qUxn0LF7Ct

Codex runs INSIDE crabbox while it is building crabbox.
This is becoming essential infra for my work.

Codex been looping nonstop for the last 4 days in multiple trees. Since all of it is e2e verifiable it basically builds itself. Codex even signs up for the services automatically via browser/computer use. My main job is adding credit card details and closing things that I don't see as a fit.

我几乎已经跟不上大家提交到 https://t.co/qUxn0LF7Ct 的那些 Issues/PR 的实现、测试和落地速度了。

Codex 在 crabbox 里面跑，而它跑的时候又在构建 crabbox。
这已经快成我工作里的关键基础设施了。

Codex 这 4 天一直在多个 tree 里不停 loop。因为这一切都能做端到端验证，它基本上已经是在自己把自己搭起来。Codex 甚至会通过 browser/computer use 自动去注册各种服务。我现在主要干的事，就是填信用卡信息，以及把那些我觉得不合适的东西关掉。
